name: Radiance Caching for Participating Media
definition: A method for efficiently computing lighting within participating media by sparsely sampling inscattered radiance ($L_s$ and $L_m$) and caching them for extrapolation, separating cache points based on the expected frequency content of the radiance values (single scattering from lights, single scattering from surfaces, and multiple scattering).
summary: Radiance caching for participating media is a view-driven Monte Carlo technique that sparsely samples and extrapolates inscattered radiance to efficiently compute lighting while concentrating samples where illumination matters most to the eye.
